title: Hero definition
description: A hero's authored definition. Ranges here are the same numbers ContentBounds enforces in the loader; SchemaAgreementTests asserts the two never drift apart.

schema_version.description: Version of this content format (TDD 11.1). Pinned by const so a file authored for a later format is refused by tooling, not read under today's assumptions; ContentSet.SupportedContentSchemaVersion states the same number and SchemaAgreementTests keeps the two equal.

id.description: Stable namespaced identifier; the pattern is ContentId's own format.

display_name_key.description: Localization key, never a player-facing literal (TDD 11.1). The pattern is the artifact-safe character set: this key travels unchanged into HeroState and from there into the canonical determinism artifact, where non-ASCII text and control characters are exactly the inputs the frozen corpus records the C# writer and RFC 8785 disagreeing on.

grade.description: How good this hero is at all, on its own scale (DEC-013, RESOLUTION_SPEC 2.2). The range coincides with the hero scales above and the constants deliberately do not: nothing divides by this span, so raising the range of greed must not raise how strong a crew is.

expertise.description: How good this hero is at each need he is answerable for. Any subset of the vocabulary, including none. A present key at 0 and a missing key are different facts: the first means the hero is answerable for that need at zero skill, the second that it is not his business (RESOLUTION_SPEC 2.2).

capability.description: What this hero can do — the layer DEC-013 keeps apart from greed, caution, pride and trust_in_guild.

traits.description: Ids of traits.schema.json entries this hero carries. Whether each id resolves to a defined trait is checked at load time, not here (Task 2).

hero.description: Id of the other hero this relationship is about.

relationships.description: One-directional opinions this hero holds about other heroes.
